## Diseases of the Ear and Mastoid Process

### Self-Reported Ear or Hearing Problems

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ear/hearing problems
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
hearing <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Chronic_Conditions.csv")

# Data wrangling
hearing <- hearing %>%
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(noear_n = total_n - ear_hearing_problems_n) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>%
  #
  dplyr::rename(yesear_n   = ear_hearing_problems_n,
                answered_n = total_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(yesear_prop   = yesear_n / answered_n * 100,
                noear_prop    = noear_n / answered_n * 100,
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("yesear"),
                starts_with("noear"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to      = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "yesear"   = "Yes",
                                              "noear"    = "No",
                                              "answered" = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Yes",
                                           "No",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 17% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne reported that they had an ear or hearing problem. This equates to approximately 6,800 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- Males were more likely to have an ear or hearing problem than females (19% vs. 16%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Definitions and notes about this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- Data for this topic were collected from all people completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey.

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- `r note_aboriginality_natsihs`

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- People were classified as having ear or hearing problems if they selected any option other than *No, don't have any hearing problems*.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Survey questions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- Do you have any hearing problems or problems with your ears that have lasted, or are expected to last, for six months or longer? (*Select all that apply*)
  - Total deafness
  - Deaf in one ear
  - Hearing impairment or partially deaf
  - Tinnitus (ringing in your ears)
  - Ménière's disease
  - Otitis media, glue ear, or middle ear infection
  - Other (please specify)
  - No, don't have any hearing problems

:::

### Hospital Admissions for Ear and Mastoid Process Diseases

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hospitalisations - ear and mastoid process diseases
# Data from PHIDU Social Health Atlas
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in PHIDU data
hospital_ear <- f_read_phidu_iare_hospital(data_sheet    = "Admissions_principal_diag",
                                           column_select = "admissions_for_ear_and_mastoid_process_diseases_aboriginal_people")

# Data wrangling
hospital_ear <- hospital_ear %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(iare_name = factor(iare_name, levels = iare_inc_vic_lvl)) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::arrange(iare_name)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Social Health Atlas of Australia](https://phidu.torrens.edu.au/social-health-atlases), compiled from the [Victorian Admitted Episodes Dataset (VAED)](https://www.health.vic.gov.au/data-reporting/victorian-admitted-episodes-dataset).

- During the four-year period 01 July 2017 to 30 June 2021 there were 362 hospital admissions for ear and mastoid process diseases for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne.

- The number of admissions for ear and mastoid process diseases for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 44 (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 7 (Knox and Whitehorse IAREs).

- The age-standardised rate of admissions for ear and mastoid process diseases for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 325 per 100,000 population (Whitehorse IARE) to 164 per 100,000 population (Knox IARE).

- 6 of the 9 IAREs in the NEPHU catchment area with data available for reporting had an age-standardised admission rate for ear and mastoid process diseases above the average rate for all Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne (Whitehorse, Melbourne/Port Phillip, Yarra Ranges, Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea, Melbourne North-East, and Craigieburn/Sunbury IAREs).

::: {.callout-tip title="Definitions and notes about this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- `r note_aboriginality_vaed`

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

`r note_caveat_admissions`

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

`r note_caveat_iare_ratio`
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="ICD-10-AM codes for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
Admissions for ear and mastoid process diseases were defined as those with a principal diagnosis code in the following list, coded using the [International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision Australian Modification (ICD-10-AM)](https://www.ihacpa.gov.au/health-care/classification/icd-10-amachiacs):

  - H60-H62: Diseases of external ear
  - H65-H75: Diseases of middle ear and mastoid
  - H80-H83: Diseases of inner ear
  - H90-H95: Other disorders of ear

:::

## Acute Ear, Nose, and Throat Infections

### Hospital Admissions for Acute Ear, Nose, and Throat Infections

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hospitalisations - acute ear, nose, and throat infections
# Data from PHIDU Social Health Atlas
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in PHIDU data
hospital_ent <- f_read_phidu_iare_hospital(data_sheet    = "Admissions_acute_prev",
                                           column_select = "admissions_for_acute_ear_nose_and_throat_infections_aboriginal_people")

# Data wrangling
hospital_ent <- hospital_ent %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(iare_name = factor(iare_name, levels = iare_inc_vic_lvl)) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::arrange(iare_name)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Social Health Atlas of Australia](https://phidu.torrens.edu.au/social-health-atlases), compiled from the [Victorian Admitted Episodes Dataset (VAED)](https://www.health.vic.gov.au/data-reporting/victorian-admitted-episodes-dataset).

- During the four-year period 01 July 2017 to 30 June 2021 there were 360 hospital admissions for acute ear, nose, and throat infections for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne.

- The number of admissions for acute ear, nose, and throat infections for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 47 (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 9 (Maroondah IARE).

- The age-standardised rate of admissions for acute ear, nose, and throat infections for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 420 per 100,000 population (Knox IARE) to 197 per 100,000 population (Yarra Ranges IARE).

- 7 of the 9 IAREs in the NEPHU catchment area with data available for reporting had an age-standardised admission rate for acute ear, nose, and throat infections above the average rate for all Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne (Knox, Moreland/Broadmeadows, Craigieburn/Sunbury, Maroondah, Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea, Melbourne/Port Phillip, and Melbourne North-East IAREs).

::: {.callout-tip title="Definitions and notes about this topic" icon=false collapse=false}

## Diseases of the Eye and Ocular Adnexa

### Self-Reported Eye or Sight Problems

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Eye/sight problems
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
eyesight <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Chronic_Conditions.csv")

# Data wrangling
eyesight <- eyesight %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(noeye_n = total_n - eye_sight_problems_n) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>%
  #
  dplyr::rename(yeseye_n   = eye_sight_problems_n,
                answered_n = total_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(yeseye_prop   = yeseye_n / answered_n * 100,
                noeye_prop    = noeye_n / answered_n * 100,
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("yeseye"),
                starts_with("noeye"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to      = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "yeseye"   = "Yes",
                                              "noeye"    = "No",
                                              "answered" = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Yes",
                                           "No",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 46% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne reported that they had an eye or sight problem (including colour blindness). This equates to approximately 18,000 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- Females were more likely to have an eye or sight problem than males (48% vs. 45%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Definitions and notes about this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- Data for this topic were collected from all people completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey.

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- `r note_aboriginality_natsihs`

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- People were classified as having an eye or sight problem if they selected that they were colour blind and/or selected any option other than *No, don't have any sight or eye problems*.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Survey questions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- Are you colour blind?
  - `r note_response_binary`

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- Do you have any other sight problems? (*Select all that apply*)
  - Astigmatism
  - Short-sightedness, myopia, difficulty seeing objects in the distance, or needing driving glasses
  - Macular degeneration
  - Other age-related sight problems or presbyopia
  - Long-sightedness, hyperopia, difficulty seeing objects close up, or needing reading glasses
  - Totally blind in both eyes
  - Totally blind in one eye
  - Partially blind in both eyes
  - Partially blind in one eye
  - Glaucoma
  - Cataracts
  - Trachoma
  - Lazy eye or strabismus
  - Retinopathy
  - Other (please specify)
  - No, don't have any sight or eye problems

:::

- During the four-year period 01 July 2017 to 30 June 2021 there were 579 hospital admissions for eye and ocular adnexa diseases for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne.

- The number of admissions for eye and ocular adnexa diseases for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 78 (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 9 (Knox IARE).

- The age-standardised rate of admissions for eye and ocular adnexa diseases for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 533 per 100,000 population (Melbourne East IARE) to 188 per 100,000 population (Knox IARE).

- 4 of the 10 IAREs in the NEPHU catchment area had an age-standardised admission rate for eye and ocular adnexa diseases above the average rate for all Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne (Melbourne East, Craigieburn/Sunbury, Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea, and Moreland/Broadmeadows IAREs).

::: {.callout-tip title="Definitions and notes about this topic" icon=false collapse=false}

  - H00-H06: Disorders of eyelid, lacrimal system, and orbit
  - H10-H13: Disorders of conjunctiva
  - H15-H22: Disorders of sclera, cornea, iris, and ciliary body
  - H25-H28: Disorders of lens
  - H30-H36: Disorders of choroid and retina
  - H40-H42: Glaucoma
  - H43-H45: Disorders of vitreous body and globe
  - H46-H48: Disorders of optic nerve and visual pathways
  - H49-H52: Disorders of ocular muscles, binocular movement, accommodation, and refraction
  - H53-H54: Visual disturbances and blindness
  - H55-H59: Other disorders of eye and adnexa

:::

## Oral and Dental Health

### Loss of Natural Teeth

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Loss of natural teeth
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
teeth <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Dental_Lost.csv")

# Data wrangling
teeth <- teeth %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(have_lost_own_natural_teeth_excl_wisdom_teeth_n:have_not_lost_any_of_own_natural_teeth_excl_wisdom_teeth_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(yes_n = have_lost_own_natural_teeth_excl_wisdom_teeth_n,
                no_n  = have_not_lost_any_of_own_natural_teeth_excl_wisdom_teeth_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(yes_n:no_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("yes_"),
                starts_with("no_"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to      = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "yes"      = "Yes",
                                              "no"       = "No",
                                              "answered" = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Yes",
                                           "No",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 53% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne had lost one or more of their natural teeth, including adults who had lost natural teeth or had them removed (excluding wisdom teeth) and children who had had teeth pulled out by a dentist. This equates to approximately 15,400 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people.

- Males were more likely to have lost one or more of their natural teeth than females (58% vs. 47%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Definitions and notes about this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- Data for this topic were collected from all people completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey.

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- `r note_aboriginality_natsihs`

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- People were classified as having lost one or more natural teeth if they answered *Yes* to losing any natural teeth or having them taken out (people aged 15 years and over) or answered *Yes* to having any teeth pulled out by the dentist (people aged less than 15 years).
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Survey questions for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
- Have you lost any of your natural teeth or had them taken out, excluding wisdom teeth?
  - `r note_response_binary`
  
<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

- Have you had any teeth pulled out by the dentist?
  - `r note_response_binary`

:::

### Hospital Admissions for Acute Oral and Dental Conditions

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hospitalisations - acute dental conditions
# Data from PHIDU Social Health Atlas
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in PHIDU data
hospital_teeth <- f_read_phidu_iare_hospital(data_sheet    = "Admissions_acute_prev",
                                             column_select = "admissions_for_acute_dental_conditions_aboriginal_people")

# Data wrangling
hospital_teeth <- hospital_teeth %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(iare_name = factor(iare_name, levels = iare_inc_vic_lvl)) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::arrange(iare_name)
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Social Health Atlas of Australia](https://phidu.torrens.edu.au/social-health-atlases), compiled from the [Victorian Admitted Episodes Dataset (VAED)](https://www.health.vic.gov.au/data-reporting/victorian-admitted-episodes-dataset).

- During the four-year period 01 July 2017 to 30 June 2021 there were 496 hospital admissions for acute oral and dental conditions for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne.

- The number of admissions for acute oral and dental conditions for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 84 (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 8 (Whitehorse IARE).

- The age-standardised rate of admissions for acute oral and dental conditions for Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in different IAREs within the NEPHU catchment ranged from 465 per 100,000 population (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea IARE) to 228 per 100,000 population (Craigieburn/Sunbury IARE).

- 5 of the 9 IAREs in the NEPHU catchment area with data available for reporting had an age-standardised admission rate for acute oral and dental conditions above the average rate for all Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in Greater Melbourne (Northcote/Preston/Whittlesea, Moreland/Broadmeadows, Melbourne East, Yarra Ranges, and Whitehorse IAREs).

::: {.callout-tip title="Definitions and notes about this topic" icon=false collapse=false}

::: {.callout-tip title="ICD-10-AM codes for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
Admissions for acute oral and dental conditions were defined as those with a principal diagnosis code in the following list, coded using the [International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems 10th Revision Australian Modification (ICD-10-AM)](https://www.ihacpa.gov.au/health-care/classification/icd-10-amachiacs):

  - K02: Dental caries
  - K03: Other diseases of hard tissues of teeth
  - K04: Diseases of pulp and periapical tissues
  - K05: Gingivitis and periodontal diseases
  - K06: Other disorders of gingiva and edentulous alveolar ridge
  - K08: Other disorders of teeth and supporting structures
  - K09.8: Other cysts of oral region, not elsewhere classified
  - K09.9: Cyst of oral region, unspecified
  - K12: Stomatitis and related lesions
  - K13: Other diseases of lip and oral mucosa
  - K14.0: Glossitis

:::
